lpp.working_capital_metric.currency_code.name: currency_code
lpp.working_capital_metric.currency_code.description: The ISO 4217 currency code in which all monetary amounts in the record are denominated; all records in the sample are reported in USD.

lpp.ach_return.description: This table records ACH (Automated Clearing House) payment returns — transactions that were initiated but subsequently returned by the receiving bank. One row represents a single ACH return event, capturing the reason for return, the originating company and bank account, and whether the return has been resolved. Key identifiers include uuid (primary key), original_transfer_ref (linking back to the originating payment), company_ref, and bank_account_ref.
lpp.ach_return.grain: One row per ACH return event received against an original ACH transfer.

lpp.acquirer.description: This table is a reference list of payment acquirers and processors that the business uses to accept card and electronic payments. One row represents a single acquirer entity, capturing its identity, regional scope, strategic classification, and the settlement account into which funds flow. Key identifiers include uuid (primary key) and code (e.g., ADYEN, STRIPE, CHASE_PAYTECH).
lpp.acquirer.grain: One row per payment acquirer or processor onboarded by the business.

lpp.acquirer_contract.description: This table stores the contractual agreements between the company's legal entities and their payment acquirers, including commercial terms such as processing margin, settlement lag, monthly minimums, and SLA commitments. One row represents a single contract between a specific company entity and an acquirer, valid for a defined effective date range. Key identifiers include uuid (primary key), acquirer_ref, and company_ref.
lpp.acquirer_contract.grain: One row per acquirer contract between a company legal entity and a payment acquirer.

lpp.acquirer_sla_metric.description: This table captures daily operational performance metrics for each payment acquirer, measured against their contractual SLA obligations. One row represents the performance of a single acquirer on a single calendar date, including authorization rates, response times, settlement punctuality, uptime, and any SLA breaches or incidents. Key identifiers are acquirer_ref and measurement_date (composite primary key).
lpp.acquirer_sla_metric.grain: One row per acquirer per measurement date reflecting that day's SLA performance metrics.

lpp.ap_invoice.description: This table records accounts payable invoices received from vendors across all legal entities in the group, tracking the full payment lifecycle from issuance through to settlement. One row represents a single vendor invoice, with amounts split across total billed, paid, and open balances along with payment status and terms. Key identifiers include uuid (primary key), invoice_number, vendor_ref, and company_ref.
lpp.ap_invoice.grain: One row per accounts payable invoice issued by a vendor to a company legal entity.

lpp.app_user.description: This table represents application users within the treasury and finance platform, storing identity and access profile information for each individual. One row corresponds to one registered user account, identified by a UUID and email address. Key identifiers include the uuid primary key, email, and the functional role code (e.g., TREAS_FRONT, CFO_GLOBAL) that governs the user's access and responsibilities.
lpp.app_user.grain: One row per registered application user account.

lpp.ar_invoice.description: This table represents accounts receivable invoices issued by group entities to customers, capturing the full lifecycle of each invoice from issuance through payment or write-off. One row corresponds to one invoice issued by a specific legal entity to a specific customer on a given date. Key identifiers include the uuid primary key, invoice_number, company_ref, and customer_ref, with amounts tracked in invoice currency.
lpp.ar_invoice.grain: One row per accounts receivable invoice issued by a legal entity to a customer.

lpp.audit_trail.description: This table records a log of all significant actions performed on key business entities within the treasury application, such as bank accounts, hedge relationships, liquidity policies, and transfers. One row corresponds to one auditable event (create, update, or approve) performed by a user on a specific entity at a specific point in time. Key identifiers include the uuid primary key, entity_type, entity_code, actor_user, and occurred_at timestamp, with before and after state snapshots stored as structured objects.
lpp.audit_trail.grain: One row per auditable action performed on a business entity by a user.

lpp.bank.description: This table is a reference directory of banking counterparties used by the treasury function, storing identification, contact, risk, and configuration attributes for each bank. One row corresponds to one bank counterparty, identified by an internal code and optionally a BIC/SWIFT code and LEI. Key identifiers include the uuid primary key, code, bic, and lei, with risk_tier_ref and cash_exposure limits used to manage counterparty risk.
lpp.bank.grain: One row per bank counterparty recognised by the treasury system.

lpp.bank_account.description: This table is the master record of all bank accounts held by group legal entities, capturing their configuration, ownership, purpose, cash management settings, and payment capabilities. One row corresponds to one bank account belonging to a specific legal entity, identified by a unique account code and linked to a bank branch. Key identifiers include the uuid primary key, code, company_ref, branch_ref, and currency_ref, with account_purpose (e.g., OPERATING, COLLECTION, PAYROLL) indicating the account's functional role.
lpp.bank_account.grain: One row per bank account held by a legal entity at a specific bank branch.

lpp.bank_account_group.description: Represents a named grouping of bank accounts used to organize accounts for reporting, pooling, or operational purposes. One row represents a single bank account group definition with a unique identifier and descriptive label. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key) and code (business reference code).
lpp.bank_account_group.grain: One row per bank account group defined in the system.

lpp.bank_account_group_member.description: Represents the many-to-many relationship between bank account groups and their individual member bank accounts. One row represents a single bank account's membership in a specific account group. Key identifiers are the composite primary key of account_group_code and bank_account_code.
lpp.bank_account_group_member.grain: One row per bank account assigned to a bank account group.

lpp.bank_account_signatory.description: Represents the authorization records defining which users or roles have signatory authority on specific bank accounts, including their role type, monetary limits, and certification status. One row represents a single signatory authorization for a given user role on a specific bank account. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key), bank_account_ref, and user_ref.
lpp.bank_account_signatory.grain: One row per signatory authority assignment linking a user role to a bank account.

lpp.bank_branch.description: Represents reference data for physical or operational bank branches, including their SWIFT/BIC codes, geographic details, processing cut-off times, and system integration identifiers. One row represents a single bank branch belonging to a parent bank institution. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key), code (e.g. BR_ANZ_SYD), bank_ref, and bic (SWIFT code).
lpp.bank_branch.grain: One row per bank branch at a specific location for a given parent bank.

lpp.bank_fee.description: Represents individual bank fee charges levied by banks against specific accounts for banking services during a statement period, including the actual charged amount, expected amount based on a negotiated rate card, and any overage. One row represents a single fee line item for a specific service code on a bank account for a given statement period. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key), bank_account_ref, bank_ref, service_code, and cash_flow_ref.
lpp.bank_fee.grain: One row per bank fee charge for a specific service on a bank account within a statement period.

lpp.bank_group.description: This table represents a named grouping of banks used for organizational or analytical purposes within the liquidity and payments platform. Each row defines a single bank group with a unique code and human-readable label. Key identifiers are the UUID primary key and the alphanumeric code.
lpp.bank_group.grain: One row per distinct bank group defined in the system.

lpp.bank_group_member.description: This table captures the many-to-many relationship between individual banks and the bank groups they belong to. Each row represents the membership of a single bank within a single bank group, acting as a bridge between bank and bank group dimensions. Key identifiers are the composite primary key of bank_group_code and bank_code.
lpp.bank_group_member.grain: One row per bank-to-bank-group membership assignment.

lpp.bank_service_type.description: This reference table defines the catalogue of banking services that can be charged or tracked, such as wire transfers, ACH credits, account maintenance, and SEPA payments. Each row describes a distinct service type with a code, display name, and functional category. Key identifiers are the alphanumeric code and the category grouping used for aggregation and pricing analysis.
lpp.bank_service_type.grain: One row per distinct bank service type offered or tracked.

lpp.bank_statement_balance.description: This table stores daily bank account balance positions as reported via bank statement feeds, capturing opening, closing, and intraday balances per account per date. Each row represents a specific balance type for a given bank account on a given statement date, sourced from BAI-format bank feed files. Key identifiers are the composite primary key of account_ref, statement_date, and balance_type, with data quality status flagged on ingestion.
lpp.bank_statement_balance.grain: One row per bank account, statement date, and balance type (opening, closing, or intraday).

lpp.benchmark_rate.description: This table stores published benchmark interest rates (such as SOFR, SONIA, ESTR, and TIIE) by date and tenor, sourced from central banks. Each row represents the annualised rate for a specific benchmark, observation date, and maturity tenor (overnight, 1-month, or 3-month). Key identifiers are the composite primary key of benchmark_code, rate_date, and tenor, with currency code indicating the rate's denomination.
lpp.benchmark_rate.grain: One row per benchmark rate code, rate date, and tenor combination.

lpp.borrowing.description: Represents individual drawdown events against corporate credit facilities, capturing the full lifecycle of each borrowing from drawdown to repayment. One row represents a single borrowing drawn under a named facility by a specific legal entity. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key), facility_ref (e.g. CF_RCF_EUR_500M), and company_ref (e.g. GR_GB).
lpp.borrowing.grain: One row per individual borrowing drawdown against a credit facility by a legal entity.

lpp.brain_evaluation.description: Records the execution and output of an AI reasoning engine ('brain') that evaluates natural language or structured queries against a knowledge graph. One row represents a single query evaluation session, capturing the seed facts, graph edges traversed, conflicts flagged, and the resulting answer summary. Key identifiers are uuid and user_code.
lpp.brain_evaluation.grain: One row per query evaluation performed by the brain reasoning engine.

lpp.budget_code.description: A small reference lookup table defining the set of high-level budget categories used across the organisation. One row represents a single budget code classification such as operating budget, capital expenditure, tax, or treasury. Key identifiers are uuid and code (e.g. BC_CAPEX).
lpp.budget_code.grain: One row per defined budget category code.

lpp.capital_allocation_actual.description: Records actual capital deployed by legal entity, reporting period, and allocation bucket (e.g. CAPEX, M&A, dividends, debt paydown, buybacks), compared against a framework target percentage. One row represents the actual capital amount allocated to a specific bucket for a given company in a given quarter. Key identifiers are the composite of company_ref, period_date, and bucket.
lpp.capital_allocation_actual.grain: One row per company, quarter-end reporting period, and capital allocation bucket combination.

lpp.card_authorization.description: Captures each card payment authorization request and its outcome, including acquirer, card network, 3DS authentication status, decline reason codes, and device fingerprint for fraud analysis. One row represents a single card authorization attempt linked to a point-of-sale transaction. Key identifiers are uuid and pos_transaction_ref, with acquirer_ref as the distribution key.
lpp.card_authorization.grain: One row per card authorization request submitted to an acquirer or payment network.

lpp.card_bin_range.description: This table is a reference lookup mapping Bank Identification Number (BIN) ranges to their associated card network, issuer, and product type. Each row represents a contiguous range of 6-digit BIN prefixes assigned to a specific card-issuing institution. Key identifiers include uuid (primary key), bin_low and bin_high defining the range, and network_code linking to the card network.
lpp.card_bin_range.grain: One row per contiguous BIN range assigned to a card issuer and product type.

lpp.card_network.description: This table is a reference lookup of payment card networks and schemes supported by the platform, such as Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and UnionPay. Each row represents a distinct card network identified by a short code, with its display name and operational type (credit, debit, charge, or private label). The primary key is the network code.
lpp.card_network.grain: One row per payment card network or scheme.

lpp.card_rebate_earning.description: This table records the actual rebate earnings generated by corporate card programs for each legal entity, spend category, and quarterly reporting period. Each row captures the eligible spend volume, rebate amount earned, currency, and the rebate tier achieved for a specific program-company-period-category combination. Key identifiers include uuid, program_ref, company_ref, and period_date.
lpp.card_rebate_earning.grain: One row per card rebate program, company, spend category, and quarterly reporting period.

lpp.card_rebate_program.description: This table defines the terms and configuration of corporate card rebate programs negotiated between the company and issuing banks. Each row represents a distinct rebate program linked to a specific bank, legal entity, and card type, including the spend threshold, rebate rate in basis points, and the effective date range. Key identifiers include uuid and code (e.g., REB_JPM_VCARD).
lpp.card_rebate_program.grain: One row per corporate card rebate program agreement between a company entity and an issuing bank.

lpp.card_settlement_batch.description: This table records the financial outcomes of card settlement batches submitted by merchants through acquiring processors to card networks. Each row represents a single settlement batch, capturing gross sales, refunds, chargebacks, interchange and network fees, processor margin, and the resulting net deposit to the merchant's bank account. Key identifiers include uuid, acquirer_ref, network_code, and bank_account_ref.
lpp.card_settlement_batch.grain: One row per card settlement batch closed by an acquirer for a specific network and merchant bank account.

lpp.card_settlement_line.description: Represents an individual line item within a card payment settlement batch, capturing the full fee breakdown for a settled card transaction. Each row corresponds to one settled card transaction line linked to a processing batch and an originating authorization, with gross amount, interchange, network assessment, processor margin, and net amounts recorded. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key), batch_ref (batch grouping), and authorization_ref (link to the original authorization).
lpp.card_settlement_line.grain: One row per individual card transaction line item within a settlement batch.

lpp.cash_balance.description: Records the end-of-day cash balance for each bank account across multiple reporting perspectives, including different date bases (transaction vs. value date) and inclusion flags for actual, intraday, confirmed, and estimated transactions. Each row represents a unique combination of account, date, date basis, and the four inclusion flags, enabling multi-view balance reporting for liquidity management. Key identifiers are account_ref and balance_date, with currency_code and cash_flow_status providing additional context.
lpp.cash_balance.grain: One row per account, balance date, date basis, and combination of actual/intraday/confirmed/estimated inclusion flags.

lpp.cash_flow.description: Captures individual cash flow transactions — both confirmed and forecasted — across all bank accounts, classifying each by flow type, budget code, counterparty, and payment rail. Each row represents a single cash movement event with amounts in both the transaction currency and the account currency, along with the FX rate applied. Key identifiers are uuid and reference, with account_ref, flow_code_ref, and counterparty_ref linking to related dimensions.
lpp.cash_flow.grain: One row per individual cash flow transaction or forecast entry for a bank account.

lpp.cash_flow_code.description: A reference lookup table defining the standardised classification codes used to categorise cash flow transactions throughout the system. Each row represents one distinct cash flow type with its short code, human-readable description, directional sign (IN/OUT), and cash flow statement category (Operations, Investing, Financing). The primary key is uuid, with the code field serving as the business key referenced by the cash_flow table.
lpp.cash_flow_code.grain: One row per distinct cash flow classification code.

lpp.chargeback.description: Tracks the full lifecycle of card payment chargebacks raised against the merchant, from initiation through resolution, including reason codes, amounts, acquirer and network details, and representment outcomes. Each row represents one chargeback case tied to an original card authorization, with status and classification fields capturing the outcome and root cause. Key identifiers are uuid and authorization_ref, with acquirer_ref, network_code, and company_ref providing dimensional context.
lpp.chargeback.grain: One row per chargeback case raised against an original card authorization.

lpp.company.description: Represents a legal entity within the corporate group, capturing its registered identity, tax and regulatory identifiers, and organisational metadata. One row corresponds to a single legal entity such as a country-level subsidiary or holding company. Key identifiers include uuid (primary key), code (e.g., GR_AU), LEI, and SEPA creditor identifier.
lpp.company.grain: One row per legal entity (subsidiary or operating company) within the corporate group.

lpp.company_financial_metric.description: Stores periodic financial performance and balance sheet metrics for each legal entity, covering income statement items (revenue, EBITDA, net income), cash flow measures, debt and equity positions, and capital structure ratios. One row represents a single company's financial snapshot for a specific reporting period and period type (quarterly or full-year). Key identifiers are company_ref, period_date, and period_type.
lpp.company_financial_metric.grain: One row per company, reporting period date, and period type (e.g., quarterly or full-year).

lpp.company_group.description: Defines named groupings of legal entities used for consolidation and reporting purposes, such as regional clusters (EMEA, APAC, LATAM) or the global group. One row represents a single named company group. Key identifiers are uuid and code (e.g., GROUP_EMEA).
lpp.company_group.grain: One row per defined company group (e.g., regional or consolidation grouping).

lpp.company_group_member.description: Resolves the many-to-many relationship between company groups and individual legal entities, indicating which companies belong to which groups for consolidation and reporting. One row represents the membership of a single legal entity within a single company group. Key identifiers are the composite of company_group_code and company_code.
lpp.company_group_member.grain: One row per company-to-company-group membership assignment.

lpp.counterparty_exposure.description: Captures daily snapshots of the organisation's credit exposure to each counterparty bank, broken down into deposits, investments, and derivative mark-to-market values. One row represents the total exposure to a specific counterparty bank on a specific reporting date. Key identifiers are as_of_date and counterparty_bank_ref, with all amounts standardised to USD.
lpp.counterparty_exposure.grain: One row per counterparty bank per reporting date snapshot.

lpp.credit_facility.description: Represents a credit facility agreement between a corporate legal entity and a lending bank, capturing the structural and financial terms of each facility. One row corresponds to a single credit facility arrangement, identified by a unique UUID and business code. Key identifiers include the facility code, company reference, lender bank reference, and currency, with attributes covering commitment amount, pricing (spread and fees), tenor dates, and benchmark rate.
lpp.credit_facility.grain: One row per credit facility agreement between a legal entity and a lending bank.

lpp.credit_rating.description: Tracks credit ratings issued by external rating agencies (Moody's, S&P, Fitch) for corporate legal entities, including the grade, outlook, and rating action at the time of each rating event. One row represents a single rating record for a specific company-agency combination at a point in time, with an is_current flag to identify the most recent active rating. Key identifiers are the company reference, agency, and as-of date.
lpp.credit_rating.grain: One row per credit rating event for a legal entity issued by a specific rating agency on a given date.

lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.description: Records each individual leg of a cross-border payment transaction, capturing the origination and destination countries, currencies, amounts, FX conversion details, fees, and payment method used. One row represents a single cross-border payment leg linked to a parent transfer, with granular cost and timing attributes including FX rate, FX spread, lifting fees, correspondent fees, and delivery timestamp. Key identifiers are the leg UUID, parent transfer UUID, and payment transaction UUID.
lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.grain: One row per individual leg of a cross-border payment transfer.

lpp.currency.description: A reference table containing master data for all currencies supported by the platform, including ISO codes, full names, decimal precision, and settlement float days. One row represents a single currency, identified by its UUID and ISO 4217 code. Additional attributes indicate whether the currency serves as the reference base and whether it should be suppressed from user-facing lists.
lpp.currency.grain: One row per ISO currency supported by the platform.

lpp.data_permission.description: Defines the data access permissions assigned to user profiles, specifying which business entities (companies or bank accounts) each access profile is authorised to view or modify. One row represents a single permission grant linking an access profile to a specific entity, with entity type distinguishing between companies and bank accounts. Key identifiers are the profile code and entity code combination.
lpp.data_permission.grain: One row per access profile and entity combination defining a data permission grant.

lpp.data_permission_profile.description: This table defines named data access permission profiles used to control which users or roles can read or write data across entities and regions. Each row represents a single permission profile with a machine-readable code and a human-readable description of its scope. Key identifiers are the UUID primary key and the profile code (e.g., PROF_GLOBAL_FULL, PROF_EMEA_RW).
lpp.data_permission_profile.grain: One row per distinct data permission profile defined in the system.

lpp.derivative_mtm.description: This table stores daily mark-to-market (MTM) valuations for derivative instruments, currently limited to FX forward contracts held by internal group entities against external bank counterparties. Each row captures the fair value of a specific derivative instrument on a specific valuation date in USD. Key identifiers are the instrument reference (e.g., FXF-0001248) and the valuation date.
lpp.derivative_mtm.grain: One row per derivative instrument per valuation date.

lpp.equity_action.description: This table records corporate equity actions executed by group holding companies, including share buybacks, regular dividends, and special dividends. Each row represents a single equity action event with its action and settlement dates, shares involved, amounts, and the named program under which it was executed. Key identifiers are the UUID and the program name, with action_type and action_date providing business context.
lpp.equity_action.grain: One row per equity action event (buyback execution, dividend declaration, or special dividend) per program.

lpp.fee_rate_card.description: This table holds the negotiated fee rates agreed between internal legal entities and their banking partners for specific banking services. Each row defines the rate applicable to a given bank, service code, and company combination, with validity dates indicating the active period of the rate. Key identifiers are the UUID, bank reference, service code, and effective date range.
lpp.fee_rate_card.grain: One row per negotiated fee rate per bank, service code, company, and effective date period.

lpp.forecast_cash_flow.description: This table contains versioned cash flow forecasts for internal legal entities, capturing projected inflows, outflows, or net flows by category (e.g., AR collections, AP disbursements, payroll, tax, capex) for future periods. Each row represents a single forecast line item for a specific entity, account, forecast period, and flow category within a named snapshot version. Key identifiers are the UUID, snapshot_id, company_ref, account_ref, forecast_date, and flow_category.
lpp.forecast_cash_flow.grain: One row per forecast snapshot, company, account, forecast date, and cash flow category combination.

lpp.forecast_snapshot.description: This table represents a versioned forecast run or publication event, capturing the metadata for each cash flow forecast snapshot produced by the forecasting model. One row defines a unique forecast cycle identified by its snapshot date, time granularity (daily or monthly), model version, and the horizon it covers. Key identifiers include snapshot_id (e.g., FC_20250801_M) and snapshot_date.
lpp.forecast_snapshot.grain: One row per forecast snapshot (a distinct forecast run defined by publication date, frequency, and horizon).

lpp.forecast_vs_actual.description: This table captures the comparison between forecasted and realized cash flow amounts at the legal entity, period, and flow category level, enabling forecast accuracy measurement and variance analysis. Each row records the forecast amount, actual amount, absolute variance, and percentage deviation for a specific company, month-end period, and cash flow type (e.g., CAPEX, AR_COLLECTION, PAYROLL). Key identifiers are company_ref, period_date, flow_category, and snapshot_id.
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.grain: One row per combination of legal entity, month-end period, cash flow category, and forecast snapshot.

lpp.fraud_detection_event.description: This table records individual fraud detection events raised by the fraud scoring system against payments or files, capturing the risk score, decision outcome, and contributing reason codes at the time of assessment. Each row represents a single fraud evaluation event linked optionally to a payment transfer or file. Key identifiers are uuid, transfer_uuid, and file_uuid.
lpp.fraud_detection_event.grain: One row per fraud detection event raised by the fraud scoring engine.

lpp.fraud_loss.description: This table records realized fraud loss incidents at the legal entity level, including the loss amount, recovery amount, fraud vector, authentication method, and classification (friendly fraud vs. true fraud). Each row represents a confirmed fraud loss event tied to a specific payment authorization and optionally linked back to a fraud detection event. Key identifiers are uuid, detection_event_uuid, and authorization_ref.
lpp.fraud_loss.grain: One row per confirmed fraud loss incident linked to a payment authorization.

lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.description: This table stores forward-looking foreign exchange exposure forecasts for each legal entity, broken down by currency pair, tenor bucket, exposure source, and direction (long or short). Each row quantifies the gross FX exposure in the exposure currency for a future period, captured at a specific snapshot date to enable vintage tracking. Key identifiers are uuid, company_ref, forecast_period, exposure_currency, and snapshot_date.
lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.grain: One row per legal entity, forecast period, tenor bucket, exposure currency, direction, source, and snapshot date.

lpp.fx_forward.description: This table represents FX forward contracts entered into by group entities to hedge currency exposure, where each record captures a single agreed deal to buy one currency and sell USD at a locked-in forward rate on a future settlement date. It tracks the full lifecycle of each contract from trade date through settlement, including counterparty bank, notional amounts, contracted rate, and spot rate at inception. Key identifiers are uuid (system key) and deal_id (business key such as FXF-0001653), with company_ref and counterparty_bank_ref as primary dimensions.
lpp.fx_forward.grain: One row per FX forward contract deal executed by a group entity with a counterparty bank.

lpp.fx_rate.description: This table stores daily foreign exchange rates between currency pairs, sourced from providers such as Bloomberg, the European Central Bank, and internal systems, covering spot and other rate types. Each row represents the exchange rate for a specific base-to-quote currency pair on a given date and rate type, enabling currency conversion across the enterprise. The composite primary key is (rate_date, base_currency, quote_currency, rate_type), making this a standard market data reference used for revaluation and reporting.
lpp.fx_rate.grain: One row per currency pair, rate date, and rate type combination.

lpp.gen_company_region.description: This is a small reference table mapping each group legal entity (company code) to its geographic region and functional currency, with 24 rows covering all subsidiaries across regions such as EMEA, APAC, LATAM, AMER, and MENA. Each row represents one legal entity within the corporate group, identified by its company_code (e.g., GR_APAC_PTE). It serves as a master data lookup to enrich other tables with regional and currency context.
lpp.gen_company_region.grain: One row per legal entity (company code) within the corporate group.

lpp.gl_account.description: This table is a master reference of all general ledger accounts defined across the group's ERP systems (SAP, NetSuite, Oracle), capturing account codes, descriptions, classifications, and their links to legal entities and physical bank accounts. Each row represents one GL account for a specific company entity, identified by uuid and structured code (e.g., '1110-GR_AU_OPERATING_1'). Key attributes include account_class (ASSET, LIABILITY, REVENUE, etc.), currency_ref, and an optional bank_account_ref for cash accounts.
lpp.gl_account.grain: One row per general ledger account per legal entity across all ERP systems.

lpp.gl_balance.description: This table stores month-end closing balances for each general ledger account across all group entities and ERP source systems, enabling period-over-period balance sheet and P&L tracking. Each row represents the closing balance of a specific GL account as of a particular month-end date, denominated in the account's native currency. The composite primary key is (gl_account_ref, balance_date, balance_type), with source_system identifying whether the data originated from SAP, NetSuite, or Oracle.
lpp.gl_balance.grain: One row per GL account reference, month-end balance date, and balance type.

lpp.gl_reconciliation.description: This table represents monthly bank-to-general-ledger reconciliation snapshots for each bank account across the group. One row captures the bank balance, GL balance, variance, and reconciliation status for a specific account at a specific month-end date. Key identifiers are uuid (record key), bank_account_ref, gl_account_ref, and as_of_date.
lpp.gl_reconciliation.grain: One row per bank account and month-end reconciliation date.

lpp.hedge_dedesignation.description: This table records the formal de-designation events for hedge accounting relationships, capturing when and why a hedge was discontinued. Each row represents a single de-designation event tied to a specific hedge relationship, company, and currency. Key identifiers are uuid, hedge_ref, and dedesignation_date.
lpp.hedge_dedesignation.grain: One row per hedge relationship de-designation event.

lpp.hedge_relationship.description: This table defines each formal hedge accounting relationship established by group entities, linking a hedging instrument (FX forward) to the underlying hedged exposure. One row represents a single hedge relationship with its full lifecycle from designation to potential de-designation or termination. Key identifiers are uuid and code (HR-XXXXXXX), with instrument_ref linking to the hedging instrument.

lpp.intercompany_transaction.description: This table records financial transactions between group entities, routed through the in-house bank, covering purposes such as funding, loans, cash pooling, dividends, royalties, and service fees. Each row represents a single intercompany transaction with its source and target entities, accounts, amounts, and settlement status. Key identifiers are uuid and reference (IC-XXXXXXX), with source_cash_flow_ref and target_cash_flow_ref linking to the underlying cash flow records.
lpp.intercompany_transaction.grain: One row per intercompany transaction between a source and target group entity.

lpp.interest_accrual.description: This table stores daily interest accrual entries generated by borrowings, investment positions, and credit facility fees across group entities. Each row represents a single interest accrual amount for a specific company, source instrument, and calendar date, classified as either income or expense. Key identifiers are uuid and source_uuid, with company_ref and accrual_date providing entity and time context.
lpp.interest_accrual.grain: One row per interest accrual entry per company, source instrument, and accrual date.

lpp.investment_instrument.description: Represents a financial instrument available for corporate treasury investment, such as money market funds, time deposits, certificates of deposit, treasuries, commercial paper, repos, and bonds. One row per unique investment instrument, identified by a system UUID and a human-readable business code (e.g., INV_MMF_0014). Key attributes include instrument type, issuer, denomination currency, coupon rate, credit rating, and maturity date.
lpp.investment_instrument.grain: One row per unique investment instrument available to the treasury portfolio.

lpp.investment_position.description: Captures daily snapshots of the treasury's investment portfolio positions across instruments, accounts, and currencies, recording face value, market value, book value, accrued interest, yield to maturity, and duration. One row per investment instrument held in a specific bank account on a given reporting date. Key identifiers include instrument_ref, bank_account_ref, company_ref, and as_of_date.
lpp.investment_position.grain: One row per investment instrument held in a specific investment bank account on a specific valuation date.

lpp.investment_transaction.description: Records individual investment transactions executed by the group treasury, capturing purchases, coupon receipts, and maturity events across instrument types such as CDs, time deposits, MMFs, and bonds. One row per investment transaction event, identified by a system UUID and linked to a specific instrument, bank account, and company. Key fields include transaction type, trade date, settlement date, amount, price, and yield at trade.
lpp.investment_transaction.grain: One row per individual investment transaction (purchase, coupon, or maturity) executed against a specific instrument.

lpp.kg_relationship.description: Stores directed relationships between pairs of business entities within a knowledge graph, capturing the relationship type, source and target entity codes and types, confidence level, and semi-structured properties. One row per directed relationship between two named entities, identified by a system UUID. Key fields include relationship_type, from_entity_code, to_entity_code, confidence, and status.
lpp.kg_relationship.grain: One row per directed relationship between a source entity and a target entity in the knowledge graph.

lpp.letter_of_credit.description: Represents letters of credit issued by banks on behalf of group legal entities, covering both commercial LCs used for trade finance (e.g., apparel imports) and standby LCs used as financial guarantees (e.g., utility deposits, insurance retention). One row per letter of credit instrument, identified by a system UUID and a structured LC number (e.g., LC-2024-00020). Key attributes include issuing bank, applicant entity, beneficiary, face and drawn amounts, currency, status, associated credit facility, and expiration date.
lpp.letter_of_credit.grain: One row per letter of credit issued on behalf of a group entity.

lpp.liquidity_policy.description: This table represents the set of internal treasury liquidity policy rules governing minimum cash buffers, operating cash floors, counterparty concentration limits, and instrument tenor caps. Each row defines a single policy rule scoped to a company or company group, with either a monetary threshold or a percentage-based limit and a validity period. Key identifiers are uuid, company_ref, company_group_ref, and policy_type.
lpp.liquidity_policy.grain: One row per liquidity policy rule applicable to a company or company group for a given effective date range.

lpp.macro_indicator.description: This table stores daily time-series observations of key macroeconomic indicators such as the Federal Funds Rate, 3-Month SOFR, US CPI, EUR/USD volatility, Geopolitical Risk Index, and Brent crude oil price. Each row captures the value of a specific indicator for a specific region on a given date, sourced from authoritative providers such as FRED, BLS, CME, or ICE. Key identifiers are the composite primary key of indicator_code, region, and as_of_date.
lpp.macro_indicator.grain: One row per macroeconomic indicator, region, and observation date.

lpp.mapping_entry.description: This table holds the individual key-value translation entries for each cross-reference mapping table, such as converting payment rail codes to AFP service codes, cash flow types to GL account classes, internal bank codes to BIC/SWIFT codes, or company codes to functional currencies. Each row represents a single source-to-target code translation within a named mapping table. Key identifiers are the composite primary key of mapping_table_code and source_value.
lpp.mapping_entry.grain: One row per source value within a given mapping table code.

lpp.mapping_table.description: This table is a registry of the available cross-reference mapping table definitions used across the platform, such as payment rail to AFP code, cash flow to GL account, bank to BIC, and company to functional currency. Each row defines a single named mapping type with its scope and a human-readable description. Key identifiers are uuid and code.
lpp.mapping_table.grain: One row per named mapping table definition.

lpp.membership_fee.description: This table records individual membership fee transactions issued to members across regional company entities, capturing the tier, channel, fee amount, payment method, and collection outcome for each fee. Each row represents a single membership fee event tied to a specific member, with statuses including collected, failed, chargeback, or refunded. Key identifiers are uuid, member_id, and company_ref.
lpp.membership_fee.grain: One row per membership fee transaction issued to a member.

lpp.payment_exception.description: This table represents individual payment exceptions detected during the processing of payment files or transfers, capturing anomalies such as bank validation failures, duplicate payments, file format errors, and OFAC compliance holds. One row corresponds to a single exception event tied to a specific payment file or transfer, tracking its detection, resolution, cost, and the user role responsible for remediation. Key identifiers include uuid (exception record), file_uuid (source payment file), and transfer_uuid (linked transfer transaction).
lpp.payment_exception.grain: One row per payment exception event detected against a payment file or transfer transaction.

lpp.payment_file.description: This table represents payment files submitted to banks, each corresponding to an ISO pain.001 XML batch file containing one or more individual payment transactions originated by a specific legal entity from a designated bank account. One row corresponds to a single payment file submission, capturing its routing and acknowledgement status, aggregate transaction count and value, and the company and account from which it was sent. Key identifiers include file_uuid, with file_name, company_ref, and account_ref providing business context.
lpp.payment_file.grain: One row per payment file submitted to the bank by a legal entity from a specific bank account.

lpp.payment_hub_throughput.description: This table captures daily operational metrics for the payment hub, summarising transaction volumes, monetary values, success and rejection counts, repair counts, and straight-through processing rates by payment rail and country. One row represents aggregated throughput statistics for a specific payment rail on a given calendar date, as originated through the Kyriba Payment Hub. Key identifiers include uuid, with metric_date and payment_rail forming the natural business key.
lpp.payment_hub_throughput.grain: One row per payment rail per calendar date for which hub throughput metrics were captured.

lpp.payment_transaction.description: This table represents individual payment transactions contained within payment files, capturing the full lifecycle of each outgoing payment from initiation through execution or rejection across multiple payment rails such as ACH, WIRE, SEPA CT, and RTP. One row corresponds to a single payment instruction from an internal legal entity account to an external counterparty, including amount, currency, execution date, and end-to-end reference for cross-system tracing. Key identifiers include uuid and end_to_end_id, with file_uuid linking each transaction to its parent payment file.
lpp.payment_transaction.grain: One row per individual payment transaction submitted within a payment file.

lpp.peer_company.description: This table is a reference list of competitor or peer companies used for benchmarking purposes, identifying publicly traded retail and e-commerce firms by their ticker symbol, sector, and competitive peer group. One row represents a single peer company entity against which the organisation benchmarks itself. Key identifiers include the code and ticker fields, both of which correspond to the company's stock exchange symbol.
lpp.peer_company.grain: One row per peer company included in the benchmarking universe.

lpp.peer_company_metric.description: This table stores periodic financial and operational metrics for peer/competitor companies used in benchmarking analysis. Each row represents a single company's reported metrics for a specific reporting period (quarterly or full-year), identified by stock ticker and period date. Key identifiers are peer_code (e.g., WMT, AMZN, HD), period_date, and period_type.
lpp.peer_company_metric.grain: One row per peer company per reporting period (quarter or fiscal year).

lpp.pension_plan.description: This table is a reference catalogue of the company's sponsored pension plans across different countries and legal entities. Each row represents a single pension plan, identified by a unique UUID and a business code (e.g., PP_US_DB), and includes plan type, sponsoring entity, jurisdiction, and enrolment status. Key identifiers are uuid and code.
lpp.pension_plan.grain: One row per pension plan sponsored by the company.

lpp.pension_valuation.description: This table records actuarial valuations of the company's defined-benefit pension plans at specific valuation dates. Each row captures the funded status, projected benefit obligation, plan asset values, actuarial assumptions, projected future contributions, and OCI impact for a given plan as of a specific date. Key identifiers are plan_ref and as_of_date.
lpp.pension_valuation.grain: One row per pension plan per actuarial valuation date.

lpp.pos_transaction.description: This table records individual point-of-sale transactions across all sales channels and company entities. Each row represents a single customer transaction at a specific timestamp, capturing the channel, location, payment method, transaction amount, currency, and optionally the associated member account. Key identifiers are uuid, with company_ref and location_code as important dimensional attributes.
lpp.pos_transaction.grain: One row per point-of-sale transaction across all channels and entities.

lpp.sme_feedback_session.description: This table tracks structured feedback sessions conducted between subject matter experts (SMEs) and interviewers, likely used to capture domain knowledge for a knowledge graph or AI enrichment process. Each row represents a single session with a specific SME, recording participants, timing, topic covered, and a link to the session transcript. Key identifiers are uuid, sme_user, and interviewer_user.
lpp.sme_feedback_session.grain: One row per SME feedback session between an expert and an interviewer.

lpp.sme_transcript_chunk.description: Represents a segmented chunk of a subject matter expert (SME) session transcript, broken into ordered pieces for vector search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows. One row captures a single text segment from a session, along with its embedding model metadata and OpenSearch index reference. Key identifiers are uuid (chunk) and session_uuid (parent session).
lpp.sme_transcript_chunk.grain: One row per segmented text chunk extracted from an SME session transcript.

lpp.stress_run_result.description: Records the outcome of a liquidity stress test run for a specific legal entity under a defined stress scenario at a given month-end date. Each row captures the minimum projected cash balance, breach date, severity classification, and threshold against which the scenario was evaluated. Key identifiers are uuid, scenario_ref, company_ref, and run_date.
lpp.stress_run_result.grain: One row per stress scenario, legal entity, and run date combination.

lpp.stress_scenario.description: A reference catalogue of defined liquidity stress scenarios used to simulate adverse conditions such as FX shocks, interest rate shifts, customer defaults, and receivables drops. Each row defines a single scenario with its code, human-readable description, risk category, and structured parameters. Key identifiers are uuid and code.
lpp.stress_scenario.grain: One row per defined stress scenario.

lpp.sweep_execution.description: Records the actual execution of cash sweep instructions, capturing the funds moved from an operating source account to a concentration or pooling target account on a given date. Each row represents one sweep event with pre- and post-sweep balances, swept amount, execution status, and links to the resulting cash flow records. Key identifiers are uuid, instruction_ref, source_account_ref, and execution_date.
lpp.sweep_execution.grain: One row per executed, skipped, or failed sweep instruction on a given execution date.

lpp.sweep_instruction.description: Defines the standing rules governing automated cash sweeps between source operating accounts and target concentration accounts, including sweep type, direction, target balance, threshold, schedule, and validity period. Each row represents a single sweep rule configuration for a specific account pair. Key identifiers are uuid and code.
lpp.sweep_instruction.grain: One row per configured sweep instruction linking a source account to a target concentration account.

lpp.third_party.description: This table represents external counterparties (vendors, suppliers, retail partners, or customers) that the organization transacts with. One row represents a single third-party entity, which may act as a creditor, debtor, or both, and may be an organization or an individual. Key identifiers are uuid (primary key) and code (business code such as TP_CUST_0001 or RETAIL_CONSUMER), with name providing the display label.
lpp.third_party.grain: One row per third-party entity (vendor, supplier, customer, or counterparty) registered in the system.

lpp.third_party_bank_account.description: This table stores bank account details for external third parties such as vendors, suppliers, or counterparties used for payment processing. One row represents a single bank account associated with a specific third party, identified by a combination of uuid and third_party_code, with currency and branch context. It supports payment routing by flagging the default account per third party.
lpp.third_party_bank_account.grain: One row per bank account registered for a third-party entity.

lpp.third_party_category.description: This table is a reference lookup defining the taxonomy of categories used to classify third-party entities. One row represents a single category type, identified by uuid and code, with a human-readable description. It is used to segment or group third parties for reporting and operational purposes.
lpp.third_party_category.grain: One row per third-party category classification code.

lpp.third_party_category_assignment.description: This bridge table records the many-to-many relationship between third-party entities and their assigned categories. One row represents a single assignment of a category code to a third-party code, with both columns forming a composite primary key. It enables flexible multi-category classification of vendors, suppliers, or counterparties.
lpp.third_party_category_assignment.grain: One row per combination of third-party entity and assigned category code.

lpp.transfer.description: This table records outbound payment transfer instructions submitted via ISO pain.001 XML files to banks and payment networks. One row represents a single payment transfer instruction, identified by uuid and transaction_number, capturing the amount, currency, value date, payment rail, processing status, and remittance references. Key identifiers include uuid, transaction_number, reference (AP/rent/tax obligation), and file_uuid linking back to the originating payment file.
lpp.transfer.grain: One row per outbound payment transfer instruction submitted to a bank or payment network.

lpp.tribal_knowledge_entity_link.description: This table represents the many-to-many association between a tribal knowledge fact and the business entities it relates to (e.g., customers, products, regions). One row captures a single entity linked to a specific fact, along with the role that entity plays in the context of that fact. Key identifiers are fact_uuid, entity_type, entity_code, and role, which together form the composite primary key.
lpp.tribal_knowledge_entity_link.grain: One row per unique combination of tribal knowledge fact, entity type, entity code, and role.

lpp.tribal_knowledge_fact.description: This table stores structured records of institutional or tribal knowledge — documented business rules, insights, or contextual facts captured from users or sessions. Each row represents a single knowledge fact with a full narrative, validity period, confidence level, lifecycle status, and references to its vector embedding for AI-driven retrieval. Key identifiers include uuid, with supplementary references to source_session, captured_by_user, and opensearch_doc_id.
lpp.tribal_knowledge_fact.grain: One row per distinct tribal knowledge fact captured in the system.

lpp.user_group.description: This table is a reference list of functional user groups that organize system users by business function, such as Treasury, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Financial Control, Internal Audit, and Platform Administration. Each row defines a single user group with a short code and a human-readable description. The primary key is uuid, with code serving as the natural business key.
lpp.user_group.grain: One row per distinct functional user group defined in the platform.

lpp.user_group_member.description: This table captures the membership assignments that associate individual users with their functional user groups such as Treasury, Accounts Payable, or Audit. Each row represents a single user-to-group membership relationship, forming the many-to-many bridge between users and groups. The composite primary key consists of user_group_code and user_code.
lpp.user_group_member.grain: One row per unique assignment of a user to a user group.

lpp.user_profile_assignment.description: This table records the access profile assignments granted to individual users or functional roles within the platform, controlling the scope and level of permissions available to each user. Each row maps a single user code to a single access profile code, such as global full access or a region-specific read-write profile. The composite primary key is formed by user_code and profile_code.
lpp.user_profile_assignment.grain: One row per unique assignment of an access profile to a user.

lpp.v_sme_transcript_chunk_indexable.description: This view represents individual text segments (chunks) extracted from recorded Subject Matter Expert (SME) sessions, prepared for semantic embedding and vector search indexing. One row corresponds to a single chunk of transcript text from a specific SME session, identified by a chunk UUID and sequenced by chunk index within its parent session. Key identifiers are chunk_uuid and session_uuid, with supporting attributes for the contributing expert, topic, and session start time.
lpp.v_sme_transcript_chunk_indexable.grain: One row per individual transcript chunk segment extracted from an SME session.

lpp.v_tribal_fact_indexable.description: This view exposes curated 'tribal knowledge' facts — informal or undocumented institutional knowledge — prepared for semantic search and embedding. Each row represents a single tribal fact with its classification, validity period, confidence level, narrative content, and linked business entities. Key identifiers include fact_uuid, with contextual attributes such as fact_type, trigger_condition, and linked_entities enabling retrieval in AI-assisted workflows.
lpp.v_tribal_fact_indexable.grain: One row per tribal knowledge fact record prepared for semantic indexing.

lpp.wcf_document.description: This table stores working capital finance documents, representing individual supplier financing instruments (such as approved invoices or purchase payables) submitted through a supply chain finance programme. Each row corresponds to a single WCF document linking a buyer company to a supplier, with a monetary amount, currency, issue and due dates, and a lifecycle status. Key identifiers are the uuid (primary key) and the human-readable document_number (e.g. WCF-0001423), with supplier_ref and buyer_company providing relationship context.
lpp.wcf_document.grain: One row per working capital finance document issued between a buyer company and a supplier.

lpp.webhook_event.description: This table captures inbound webhook events received from external or internal systems, recording each notification triggered by business process state changes such as payment file status updates, document approvals, or batch executions. One row represents a single webhook event delivery, identified by uuid, with the event_type, the referenced entity (entity_type and entity_code), full payload, and timestamps for when it was received and processed. It serves as an audit log and integration event store for payment file lifecycle changes.
lpp.webhook_event.grain: One row per inbound webhook event received from an integrated system.

lpp.working_capital_metric.description: This table stores periodic working capital efficiency metrics per legal entity, capturing key treasury KPIs such as Days Sales Outstanding (DSO), Days Payable Outstanding (DPO), Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO), and the Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC) alongside underlying AR/AP balances and trailing twelve-month revenue and COGS figures. Each row represents a single company's reported metrics for a specific period-end date, with the composite primary key of company_ref and period_date. It supports benchmarking, trend analysis, and working capital optimisation initiatives across the group.
lpp.working_capital_metric.grain: One row per legal entity per reporting period date for working capital KPI metrics.

0.description: This cluster represents the payments and fraud domain, centred on customer-facing financial transactions across point-of-sale channels and membership fee collections. It contains data on individual POS transactions, membership fee events (including payment outcomes such as chargebacks and refunds), and confirmed fraud loss incidents linked to specific payment authorizations. Analysts can use this community to investigate fraud patterns by channel or authentication method, reconcile membership fee collection performance, and assess the financial impact of friendly fraud versus true fraud across legal entities.

2.description: This cluster represents the FX risk management, hedging, and corporate financial structure domain, bringing together legal entity hierarchies, financial performance metrics, debt facilities, credit ratings, and FX derivative positions. It contains data on FX forward contracts, derivative mark-to-market valuations, forward-looking FX exposure forecasts, equity actions, acquirer contracts, and card rebate programs, all anchored to the corporate group and entity structure. Analytical questions it supports include hedge effectiveness monitoring, FX exposure coverage analysis, counterparty credit risk assessment, consolidated financial performance reporting, and capital structure evaluation across the group.

3.description: This cluster represents the cash flow forecasting and variance analysis domain, supporting the full lifecycle of treasury cash flow projections from model execution through to accuracy measurement. It contains versioned forecast snapshots, individual forecast line items by entity and flow category, actual cash flow transactions classified by standardised codes and budget categories, and daily payment hub throughput metrics. Analysts can use this community to compare forecast versus actual cash flows, assess forecasting model accuracy by period and flow type, and monitor payment rail performance alongside liquidity planning assumptions.

4.description: This cluster represents the cash and liquidity management domain, consolidating bank account balances, card acquiring operations, intercompany funding flows, and GL reconciliation data across all group entities. It contains daily bank statement and cash balance positions, card authorization and settlement data, chargeback records, ACH return events, intercompany transactions routed through the in-house bank, and month-end GL balances. This community enables analysts to answer questions about intraday and end-of-day liquidity positions, card acquiring performance and dispute rates, intercompany funding efficiency, and the accuracy of cash balances relative to general ledger records.

6.description: This cluster represents the treasury investment portfolio and GL reconciliation domain, tracking the group's short-term investment activity and its alignment with general ledger records. It contains daily investment position snapshots and individual transaction events across instrument types such as CDs, time deposits, and money market funds, alongside GL account master data, month-end GL balances, and monthly bank-to-GL reconciliation snapshots. Analysts can use this community to monitor portfolio yield and duration, track investment transaction activity by instrument and entity, and identify reconciling items between bank-reported positions and the general ledger.

7.description: This cluster represents the platform governance, user access management, and AI-powered knowledge graph domain, covering both operational access controls and institutional knowledge capture. It contains user identity and role records, data permission profiles and their assignments, audit trail logs of treasury application actions, and a knowledge graph layer comprising tribal knowledge facts, SME session transcripts, entity relationships, and AI brain evaluation outputs. This community supports questions around user access auditing, permission governance, and the retrieval and validation of institutional knowledge used to enrich AI reasoning over treasury and finance data.

9.description: This cluster represents the banking counterparty and account management domain, serving as the foundational reference layer for the treasury's banking relationships. It contains master data for banks, bank branches, and bank accounts (including groupings and account-to-group memberships), negotiated fee rate cards, actual bank fee charges, third-party payment account details, and macroeconomic indicator time series. Analysts can use this community to monitor bank fee costs versus negotiated rates by service type and entity, manage counterparty bank relationships and groupings, and contextualise treasury activity against macroeconomic conditions such as benchmark interest rates or FX volatility.

11.description: This cluster represents the working capital management domain, tracking the efficiency and financial flows of accounts payable, accounts receivable, and related corporate financing activity. It contains AP and AR invoice records with full payment lifecycle data, periodic working capital KPIs such as DSO, DPO, and the cash conversion cycle, corporate card rebate earnings by spend category, and individual credit facility drawdown events. This community enables analysis of payment terms compliance, working capital efficiency benchmarking across entities, the financial value generated by card rebate programs, and the relationship between short-term borrowing activity and underlying cash flow dynamics.

12.description: This cluster represents the cross-reference and code translation reference layer of the treasury and payments platform. It contains the registry of named mapping table definitions (such as payment rail to AFP code, bank code to BIC/SWIFT, cash flow type to GL account class, and company code to functional currency) alongside the individual key-value translation entries that power those mappings. Analysts can use this cluster to understand what code translations are available across the platform, audit specific source-to-target value mappings, and support data normalization or validation efforts across payment, banking, and accounting domains.
